MUJAHID:v1p374/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p374/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p374/r1.claim: Mujahid says the two parties were from among the people of the youths, and the phrase about calculating the duration means counting how long they stayed.

MUQATIL:18:11-12/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:11-12/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:11-12/r2.claim: The two groups are the believers and the polytheists; God awakens the youths so it becomes known which group better counted their stay.

MUQATIL:18:11-12/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:11-12/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:11-12/r3.claim: Amad means a set term or appointed duration.

MUQATIL:18:11-12/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:11-12/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:11-12/r4.claim: The believers who recorded the youths' story knew their duration better than the unbelievers; after the youths awoke, the whole town embraced Islam.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r4.claim: Qatāda takes the appointed duration as the endpoint when they were awakened; neither the unbelievers nor believers knew how long it was.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r5.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r5.claim: Ibn Mujāhid's father glosses the duration as a count, unknown to them.

TAB-FULL:v15p176/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r2.claim: God awakened them so people could determine which of the two disputing groups most accurately calculated the period they had slept; amad means the endpoint or term.

TAB-FULL:v15p176/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the two groups as parties from the youths' own people.

TAB-FULL:v15p176/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r4.claim: Some authorities say both groups among the people were unbelievers; others say one group was Muslim and the other unbelieving.

TAB-FULL:v15p176/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r5.claim: Qatada says neither group, whether unbelievers or believers, knew the youths' duration of sleep.

TAB-FULL:v15p176/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p176/r6.claim: The poet al-Nābigha uses amad for the goal or limit reached in a race.

TAB-FULL:v15p177/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p177/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p177/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses amad as something distant or long in duration.

TAB-FULL:v15p177/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p177/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p177/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses amad as a number or count.

TAB-FULL:v15p177/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p177/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p177/r3.claim: The accusative amad is best read as an explanatory specification of ahsa, meaning which group most accurately counted their duration, because exegetes support this interpretation.

TAB-FULL:v15p177/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p177/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p177/r4.claim: The alternative parses amad as the object of labithu, giving the sense of the endpoint of their stay.

ZAJJAJ:v3p271#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p271#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p271#2/r1.claim: Al-amad means a limit or term; its accusative may be a specification, governed by أحصى, or linked with لبثوا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p271/r3.claim: God raised them from sleep; anyone brought from death to life or sleep to wakefulness is called raised and released from restraint.

NAHHAS:v2p448/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p448/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p448/r10.claim: The two groups are the Cave companions and the people alive when the companions awoke; ‘which’ is the subject and ‘counted more’ its predicate.

NAHHAS:v2p448/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p448/r11.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p448/r11.claim: He parses ‘a duration’ as either an explanatory accusative or governed by ‘their remaining’; the author prefers the first because it fits the sense.

NAHHAS:v2p448/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p448/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p448/r12.claim: Separating ‘counted’ from ‘a duration’ is acceptable because the construction contains a verb, unlike a bare numeral and noun.

NAHHAS:v2p448/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p448/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p448/r8.claim: God ‘raised them’ means woke them from sleep; His stated purpose is a challenge, since He already knew which group counted the duration more accurately.

NAHHAS:v2p448/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p448/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p448/r9.claim: The best explanation of ‘so We may know’ is a challenge, like demanding proof from someone making a false claim; another view calls it knowledge by witnessing.

THALABI:v6p157/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r13.claim: God awakens them so the two groups can be tested over which better reckoned the time they remained asleep in the cave.

THALABI:v6p157/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r14.claim: The earlier Muslim group says the youths stayed 309 years, while a later group disputes the duration; the earlier group finally says God knows best.

THALABI:v6p157/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r15.claim: The two parties are the two groups; ahsa means more accurate or better at remembering, and amad means an endpoint.

THALABI:v6p157/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r16.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p157/r16.claim: Mujahid glosses amad as a number or count.

THALABI:v6p157/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r17.claim: The accusative on amad can be parsed either as specification or as governed by the preceding phrase about how long they stayed.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r21.claim: Their being raised means that they were awakened from their sleep.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r22.claim: لنعلم means that God looked to see which of the two parties best reckoned their stay.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r24.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r24.claim: أحصى may mean an appointed term or deadline.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r25.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r25.claim: أحصى may mean the endpoint or limit.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r26.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r26.claim: The two parties may be the people of the youths' community who disagreed about their case.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r27.claim: Alternatively, the two parties may be the youths and the people of their era who encountered them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r28.claim: Alternatively, one party is believers and the other disbelievers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r29.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p286#2/r29.claim: A further interpretation contrasts God with creation, rhetorically asking whether they or God know better.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r1.claim: God raised the youths from their sleep, meaning He woke them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r10.claim: The author finds the reported explanations of the two parties unconvincing because none resolves the ambiguity.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r2.claim: They gloss li-naʿlama as so that We may see; the commentary refers to parallel discussions in al-Baqara and Al Imran.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r3.claim: Ayy is nominative as a subject with ahṣā as predicate, while the object of knowing is implicit in the story; it behaves like asking which person stood.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r4.claim: Ayy is interrogative and cannot be governed by a preceding word except through a preposition; the commentary will revisit the construction under Maryam.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r5.claim: He identifies the two parties as successive rulers of the city on one side and the cave youths on the other.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r6.claim: He says the two parties were groups from the youths' own people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r7.claim: He identifies the two parties as believers and unbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r8.claim: He transmits a view that two groups of Muslims in the youths' era disputed how long the youths remained in the cave; its adherents distinguish the earlier Muslims from converts who saw them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r9.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p540/r9.claim: He says the youths' own dispute about their duration was the reason God raised them, while affirming that God already knows everything and no event causes Him to learn it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r1.claim: He says both parties were groups among the youths: some rejected the claim that they slept a day or part of a day, showing disagreement among them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r2.claim: The author calls this reading remote: the wording about knowing which party counted the duration does not naturally mean that God raised them to cause a dispute among themselves.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r3.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وغيرهما
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r3.claim: They understand the parties as believers and unbelievers from the youths' people, who disputed the duration; God raised the youths to clarify it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r4.claim: He allows amadan either as a specification of ahsa or as the duration object of labithu.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r5.claim: He similarly allows amadan as a specification governed by ahsa or as an object governed by labithu.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r6.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p542/r6.claim: He rejects the specification parse: ahsa is a past verb, not a regular comparative, and the duration is not the semantic subject expected for a specification; it is instead an object.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r3.claim: God awakened them from sleep so it would become known which group best counted their time in the cave.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r4.claim: Groups of believers and unbelievers had disputed how long the youths were missing and how long they had been gone.

JISHUMI:v6p4347/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r7.claim: A ḥizb is a group or band; the two parties are groups differing over their affair, and amad is the goal or limit.

JISHUMI:v6p4347/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r8.speaker: النابغة
JISHUMI:v6p4347/r8.claim: His line about the racer reaching the amad witnesses the word's sense of a limit or finish.

JISHUMI:v6p4348/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4348/r2.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v6p4348/r2.claim: He gives two possible governors for أمدا: أحصى or لبثوا; on the former analysis, the parties count the duration of their stay.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r3.claim: God raised them from their sleep, and the stated purpose is knowledge by observation; villagers had disputed how long they stayed.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r4.claim: Aḥṣā is explained as better preserving how long they remained asleep, and amad as an endpoint.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p155#2/r5.claim: He glosses amad as a number, functioning as an explanatory accusative.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r1.claim: Ay carries an interrogative sense that suspends the verb la-naʿlama; in the reading li-yaʿlama it is likewise suspended because the subject is the proposition, not an object governed by the verb.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r2.claim: The two parties may be the sleepers who disagreed after waking about their time asleep, as narrated in 18:19, or two outside groups who disputed it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r3.claim: Aḥṣā is a past verb meaning which party counted or determined the duration of their stay.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r4.claim: Reading aḥṣā as a comparative is unsound: comparative formation from a non-triliteral verb is irregular, it cannot govern amadan, and an ellipsis to rescue it is contrived.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p660/r5.claim: God did not seek to learn something unknown; He intended the truth about the duration to become manifest when the sleepers awoke, increasing faith and reflection, helping believers, and serving as a clear sign to unbelievers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#2/r1.claim: Amad is glossed as a number, an approximate explanation by meaning, following the Mujahid attribution at the preceding segment boundary.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#2/r2.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari makes amad the object of labithu, a grammatical analysis the author rejects as untenable.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r10.claim: Amad means an endpoint and can refer to a duration because a duration has a limit.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r4.claim: To raise or send forth means to set in motion after stillness, whether a person was physically still or merely inactive in the relevant matter.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r5.claim: 'So that We might know' means bringing the matter into existence, not acquiring knowledge, since God already knew which group best reckoned the duration; al-Zuhri reads the verb with yāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r6.speaker: الجمهور من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r6.claim: The apparent two groups are the youths, who thought they had slept briefly, and the townspeople alive when they awoke, who had preserved a record of them.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r7.claim: Some identify the two groups as believers, but the author says that reading does not fit the verse's wording.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r8.claim: He takes ahsā as a past-tense verb with amad as its object; al-Zajjaj instead analyzes ahsā as a superlative and amad as specification, a construction the author says is unusual for a quadriliteral verb.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p500/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj analyzes ahsā as a superlative and amad as an accusative of specification; the author notes examples that support such superlatives from quadriliteral verbs.

TABRISI:18:10-12/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:10-12/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:10-12/r10.claim: The two groups may be believers and unbelievers among the people of the cave, or the youths themselves after waking, since they disputed how long they had slept; the dispute is reflected in 18:19.

TABRISI:18:10-12/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:10-12/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:10-12/r9.claim: God woke them so the two groups could determine how long they had stayed; the event makes God’s previously known matter manifest, rather than adding knowledge to Him.

TABRISI:18:9-12#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:9-12#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:9-12#2/r1.claim: If a past verb is intended, amadan is the object of aḥṣā: the question is which party counted a period for their stay.

TABRISI:18:9-12/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:9-12/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:9-12/r7.claim: A party is a group and amad is an endpoint; al-Nābigha’s racing line uses amad for the finish or limit.

TABRISI:18:9-12/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:9-12/r9.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:18:9-12/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects parsing amadan as a specification (tamyīz): if a past verb is intended, the word is its object, meaning which party counted a period of their stay.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r1.claim: Being raised applies both to moving from death to life and from sleep to wakefulness, because the restraint on action has ended.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r2.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r2.claim: The years were complete years without months or days.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r3.claim: The two parties are the believers and unbelievers from the people of the Companions of the Cave.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r4.claim: Some interpret the purpose as letting people know which party better reckoned the period.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r5.speaker: أبو الجوزاء وأبو عمران والنخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r5.claim: They read the verb in the passive, meaning it should be known which party better reckoned the duration.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r6.claim: The two parties disputed how long the youths had remained in the cave after leaving their people; God raised them to disclose the answer.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r7.claim: Neither believers nor unbelievers among the two parties knew how long the youths had stayed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r8.claim: Once the youths were raised, doubt ended and the actual duration became known.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r9.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p114#2/r9.claim: The raising made the known disagreement over duration manifest, providing a lesson.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r1.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbās, says the two parties are successive rulers of the city and the Sleepers.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r10.claim: Wali means near: the servant draws near through obedience and sincerity, while God draws near through mercy and bounty; this relation is sainthood.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the two parties as factions among the youths, divided after waking over how long they had slept; 19:19 is his evidence.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says two Muslim groups in the Sleepers’ era disputed the length of their stay.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī rejects reading aḥṣā as a comparative adjective: this pattern is not regular for derived verbs, and exceptions cannot establish a rule.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r5.claim: He parses aḥṣā as a past verb and predicate; the clause is the object of naʿlam, amadan its object, and mā in limā is a verbal noun, yielding “which group counted the duration.”

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r6.claim: Sufi scholars use this episode as clear Qurʾānic evidence that saints’ extraordinary gifts are possible.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r7.claim: A wali may mean an active intensive: someone whose obedience continues without interruption by sin.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, wali can be passive: someone whom God continually protects from sin and sustains in obedience.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71#2/r9.claim: The name wali comes from Qurʾānic descriptions of God as the ally of believers and the righteous.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r3.claim: “Then We raised them” means God woke the youths after their sleep.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r4.claim: The purpose particle in “so that We might know” supports Rāzī’s view that God’s acts are directed to purposes.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r5.speaker: هشام
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r5.claim: Hishām argues from the apparent wording that God knows events only when they occur; Rāzī says the issue was discussed earlier and cites parallel formulations.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r6.claim: In the standard reading, ay is nominative as a subject and aḥṣā its predicate; the full clause is the object of divine knowledge, explaining its case.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r7.claim: A passive reading, li-yuʿlama, avoids attributing newly acquired knowledge to God and makes the purpose that some created observers learn.

RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p71/r8.claim: For the passive reading, ay would be expected in the accusative; an answer says grammatical markers can jointly identify one constituent.

RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r1.claim: An extraordinary event accompanied by a claim may involve divinity, prophethood, sainthood, or magic and service to demons.

RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r2.claim: The Ashʿarī position allows marvels even for one falsely claiming divinity, citing reports about Pharaoh and the Dajjāl; their outward form already exposes the lie and prevents confusion.

RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r3.claim: A true prophet must receive miracles; a false claimant cannot receive an unopposed miracle, and any apparent one must be met with opposition.

RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r4.claim: Ashʿarīs disagree about whether a saint may claim sainthood and then receive a marvel matching the claim.

RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r5.claim: Ashʿarīs allow extraordinary acts by claimants to magic or demonic service, while Muʿtazilites forbid them.

RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r6.claim: Without a claim, an extraordinary event for a righteous person is a karāma; Ashʿarīs permit it, while Muʿtazilites deny it except Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Baṣrī and Maḥmūd al-Khwārizmī.

RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p72/r7.claim: An extraordinary event appearing for a wicked person disobedient to God is called istidrāj.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r1.claim: The third infant in the report rejects his mother’s wish that he resemble a handsome tyrant, then wishes to resemble a falsely accused woman; he explains the man was oppressive and she innocent.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar transmits the Prophet’s well-known cave report: three men trapped by a rock ask God to rescue them through sincere good deeds.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r3.claim: One man’s devoted care for elderly parents opens the rock; a second leaves his cousin and her money untouched out of fear of God; their prayers shift the stone but do not yet free them.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r4.claim: A third man preserved an absent worker’s wages, invested them until they became great wealth, and later gave the worker all of it; the rock opens and they escape.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v21p73#2/r5.claim: A prophetic report says that an unregarded, disheveled believer may swear by God and have the oath fulfilled.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r1.claim: Mary’s story is another proof of saintly marvels, but Rāzī refers readers to his discussion in Āl ʿImrān.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r2.claim: The youths remained alive and unharmed through 309 years of sleep, shielded from the sun; Rāzī treats this as a karāma.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r3.claim: Some invoke the person who brought the throne before Solomon’s glance, but Rāzī identifies that person as Solomon, so the inference to a saintly wonder fails.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that a prophet must have been present in that era for the extraordinary sleep to count as a prophetic miracle.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r5.claim: Rāzī replies that the sleep itself was ordinary, and its truth could not be verified until the exact sleepers were recognized after 309 years; therefore it cannot be a prophet’s miracle but is a gift to saints.

RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v21p73/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits a report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections: only three infants spoke, including Jesus and the child who vindicated the ascetic Jurayj when he was falsely accused.

RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib transmits from Abū Hurayra that a cow carrying a load spoke, saying it was made for plowing; the Prophet and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar affirmed belief in this report.

RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r2.claim: A man hears a cloud instructed to water a named garden; its owner says he divides the harvest into thirds for family, the poor and traveler, and reinvestment.

RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r3.claim: A report about Abū Bakr says his funeral was carried to the Prophet’s tomb, the door opened, and a voice from within welcomed the beloved to the beloved.

RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r4.claim: ʿAlī says that when ʿUmar warned “Sāriya, the mountain” during Friday preaching, an army messenger later reported that the soldiers heard and obeyed the call, defeating their enemy.

RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r5.claim: An unnamed preacher calls ʿUmar’s distant sight a prophetic miracle, reasoning that ʿUmar was like the Prophet’s sight.

RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r6.claim: A report says the Nile used to stop each year until a beautiful girl was cast into it.

RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r7.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r7.claim: When an earthquake struck Medina, ʿUmar struck the ground and commanded it to be still by God’s leave; it stopped and no further quake occurred there.

RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r8.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v21p74/r8.claim: ʿUmar wrote a command to a fire on a shard, and it went out when the shard was thrown into the flames; a separate report says ʿUthmān’s first drop of blood landed on a Qurʾānic verse after he was stabbed.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r1.claim: A Roman king’s envoy saw ʿUmar sleeping on bare earth, considered killing him, then saw two lions emerge; he later embraced Islam. Rāzī calls these reports individually transmitted.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r10.claim: A report says Khālid ibn al-Walīd ate a handful of poison while invoking God’s name and was unharmed.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r11.claim: Ibn ʿUmar drove away a lion that had stopped travelers and said people are dominated by what they fear; one who fears only God should not be dominated by anything.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r12.speaker: العلاء بن الحضرمي
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r12.claim: A prophetic-era expedition led by al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī crossed a stretch of sea on foot after invoking God’s greatest name.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r13.claim: Sufi books contain many additional reports of this kind.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r2.claim: Rāzī says the historically certain marvel is that ʿUmar ruled east and west with extraordinary political success despite rejecting luxury and pretension.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r3.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r3.claim: Anas reports that ʿUthmān noticed traces of illicit looking on a visitor and called it true insight, not revelation.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r4.claim: When ʿUthmān was stabbed, the first drop of blood landed on the Qurʾānic words “God will suffice you against them.”

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r5.claim: A report says the disease that later affected Jurjah al-Ghifārī’s knee began after he broke ʿUthmān’s staff over it.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r6.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r6.claim: After ʿAlī lawfully cut a Black man’s hand for theft, the man praised the justice that saved him from hellfire; Salman relayed this, and ʿAlī prayed and restored the hand.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r7.speaker: سفينة
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r7.claim: Safīna, the Prophet’s freedman, says that after a shipwreck a lion guided him from shore when he identified himself as the Prophet’s companion.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r8.speaker: ثابت
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r8.claim: Thābit transmits from Anas that the staffs of Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and another Anṣārī glowed in the dark while they walked from the Prophet, lighting each man’s way after they parted.

RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r9.speaker: خالد بن الوليد
RAZI-FULL:v21p75/r9.claim: When Khālid found a soldier with a wineskin who claimed it held vinegar, he prayed that it become vinegar; the soldiers then found vinegar inside.

RAZI-FULL:v21p76#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p76#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p76#2/r1.claim: Fourth argument: harming God’s wali is treated like harming God, just as the Prophet’s pledge, pleasure, and harm are linked to God; feeding and visiting a believer likewise count as serving God, so small marvels are plausible.

RAZI-FULL:v21p76#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p76#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p76#2/r2.claim: Fifth argument: intimacy with an earthly king can bring unusual powers; closeness to the Lord of all worlds makes saintly wonders still more plausible and spiritually insignificant by comparison.

RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r1.claim: First rational argument: God and servant are each described as wali, and each as loving the other; when a servant obeys fully, it is fitting that God once grant the servant’s wish, as promised in the cited verse.

RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r2.claim: Second argument: denying karāma implies either God lacks the power to grant it or the believer is unworthy; both fail, since knowledge and love of God are greater gifts than bread, a tamed snake, or lion.

RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p76/r3.claim: Third argument: the divine saying about obligatory acts followed by supererogatory devotion describes God as the beloved servant’s hearing and sight; this station exceeds feeding him or controlling an animal.

RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r1.claim: Seventh argument: the human spirit is not corruptible matter but kin to angelic spirits; bodily absorption makes it forget its origin and weakens its power.

RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r2.claim: Knowledge and love of God, reduced bodily absorption, and illumination from holy celestial spirits strengthen the soul to act on worldly bodies; these acts are karāmāt.

RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r3.claim: Human spirits differ in strength and purity just as angels do; Gabriel is described as powerful and trusted, unlike angels whose intercession has no effect.

RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r4.speaker: منكرو الكرامات
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r4.claim: The first objection says God made an extraordinary occurrence a proof of prophethood, so allowing one for a non-prophet would separate the proof from its conclusion.

RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r5.speaker: منكرو الكرامات
RAZI-FULL:v21p77#2/r5.claim: The second objection appeals to the report that obligatory worship is the greatest approach to God: if those fulfilling obligations receive no marvel, those doing extra worship should receive none either.

RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r1.claim: Sixth argument: spirit, not body, is the agent; divine knowledge strengthens the soul as the soul animates the body, explaining why those more aware of the unseen have stronger hearts.

RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r2.claim: ʿAlī said he removed Khaybar’s gate by divine rather than bodily strength, as his attention had turned from bodies toward the angelic realm.

RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p77/r3.claim: When sustained worship makes God the servant’s hearing, sight, and hand, the servant can hear and see far away and act across difficult or distant things.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r1.speaker: منكرو الكرامات
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r1.claim: A third objection says miraculous travel contradicts the verse that describes burdensome journeys, noting that even the Prophet needed many difficult days to travel from Mecca to Medina.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r10.claim: The same customary-rule answer addresses the objection about evidence for a claimant.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r11.claim: Truly obedient servants are few, so their rare marvels do not undermine the claim that such events break ordinary patterns.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r2.speaker: منكرو الكرامات
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r2.claim: A fourth objection asks whether a wonder-working saint’s claim to money requires evidence: accepting it without proof conflicts with the rule that a claimant must prove his case.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r3.speaker: منكرو الكرامات
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r3.claim: A fifth objection says that if marvels appear for many saints, repeated exceptions become customary and undermine both miracle and karāma.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r4.claim: Some authorities forbid a saint to claim sainthood: unlike public prophethood, knowledge of sainthood neither saves others from unbelief nor guides them, so claiming it serves ego.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r5.claim: Those who permit such a claim distinguish it because an extraordinary event signals freedom from sin; alongside a prophetic claim it supports prophethood, and alongside sainthood it supports sainthood.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r6.claim: They add that a prophet claims and certifies a required miracle, while a saint’s wonder is not obligatory and need not be certain or protected from opposition.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r7.claim: If the saint professes adherence to a prophet when claiming a wonder, it becomes a miracle supporting that prophet rather than challenging his mission.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r8.claim: Obligatory worship alone is more complete than supererogatory worship alone, but a saint performs both and thus exceeds one who performs only obligations.

RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p78/r9.claim: The travel verse concerns ordinary customary experience, whereas saintly marvels are rare and therefore exceptions to its general rule.

RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r1.claim: Getting what one wants, whether ordinarily or extraordinarily, does not prove divine rank; it may be honor or a means of entrapment.

RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r2.claim: Istidrāj is God’s granting a sinner’s worldly wishes, which intensifies desire and indulgence in a feedback loop and gradually increases distance from God and knowledge.

RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r3.claim: The Qurʾān also names this divine entrapment mكر, kayd, and imlā; Rāzī cites verses for each usage.

RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r4.claim: A further form is destruction after apparent success, as in the people who rejoiced in their gifts and Pharaoh’s arrogant forces.

RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r5.claim: A true saint grows more afraid when a wonder appears, suspecting entrapment; one trapped by istidrāj feels entitled, grows arrogant, and becomes secure from punishment, signaling that the gift was not a karāma.

RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p79/r6.claim: Rāzī says realized scholars have often fallen away precisely amid marvels, so they fear wonders as they fear afflictions.

RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r1.claim: First proof against delighting in a wonder: joy presumes one deserves it, though no creature has a claim upon God; joy should center on the Giver and His generosity.

RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r2.claim: Second proof: a marvel is something other than God, so rejoicing in it is rejoicing in what veils a person from God.

RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r3.claim: Third proof: treating one’s deeds as inherently valuable is ignorance, since every act, gratitude, and human knowledge falls short beside God’s majesty and gifts.

RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq says an accepted deed leaves the servant’s own sight: what remains in one’s view is rejected, and what vanishes is raised and accepted.

RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r5.claim: Fourth proof: a wonder comes through humility; pride destroys the very quality that led to it, so its path ends in its own loss.

RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p80/r6.claim: When the Prophet listed his merits, he concluded “no boasting”: his pride was in the Giver, not in the gifts.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r1.claim: The youths were raised from sleep; one awakened or revived is called mabʿuth because sleep prevents movement and action.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r10.claim: Mujahid glosses amadan as a number, an approximate interpretation by meaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r11.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r11.claim: Al-Tabari makes amadan governed by the verb labithu; Ibn Atiyya rejects this analysis, while noting a possible analogy from rare quadriliteral forms.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r12.claim: A dangling citation describes the Prophet's basin water as whiter than milk and quotes Umar saying it is more neglected than its counterpart.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r2.claim: Linaʿlama means bringing God's already-known fact into existence and observation, not acquiring new knowledge; God already knew which party counted the duration better.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r3.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r3.claim: Al-Zuhri reads the verb in the passive-person form liyʿlama, with yāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r4.speaker: الجمهور من المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r4.claim: The apparent two parties are the youths, who thought they had slept briefly, and the townspeople alive when they awoke, who had records of their story.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r5.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r5.claim: One group identifies the parties as two groups of unbelievers disputing how long the sleepers remained.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r6.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r6.claim: Another group identifies the parties as two groups of believers; other proposals lack connection to the verse's wording.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r7.speaker: أبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r7.claim: Abu Ali parses amadan as a direct object.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ parses amadan as a specification accusative.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r9.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:18:12/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses amadan as an adverb of time, the endpoint of their stay.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r1.claim: God awakened the sleepers so His eternal knowledge would become manifest in a present event, not because He newly learned something.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r2.claim: The two parties disagreeing about the duration may be among the youths or outsiders; ahsa can mean measured or recorded the length of their stay.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r3.claim: The parsing may make amadan the object of ahsa and the duration phrase a circumstantial or purposive phrase; another analysis makes the duration phrase the object and amadan a specification.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:12-13/r4.claim: Another analysis treats ahsa as a comparative noun with a deleted prefix, while amadan is governed by an implied verb; a cited Arabic verse illustrates that construction.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r1.claim: God awakened them; the two groups differed about how long they slept, with the ones saying 'God knows' realizing the duration was long, or the groups may be outsiders debating it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r2.claim: Aḥṣā is a past-tense verb and amad is its adverb or object; together with its subject it fills the two complements of 'we know,' meaning which group best measured or comprehended the duration.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r3.claim: Taking aḥṣā as the superlative 'best at counting' is mistaken because forming it from a non-triliteral verb is not analogical.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p5#2/r4.claim: 'So that We may know' means making the result known to them, increasing their faith and reflection, and providing a clear sign to unbelievers; alternatively, God actualizes their disagreement already known to Him.

QASHANI:18:12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:12/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:12/r1.claim: Their raising means waking from bodily slumber, rising from the body's resting place, and knowing God and their immaterial selves; God's knowledge becomes manifest in them or others.

QASHANI:18:12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:12/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:12/r2.claim: People disagree over when the sleepers reappear: some say after a thousand years, a day with God; others after seven hundred or one hundred years, reckoned as part of a day.

QASHANI:18:12/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:12/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:12/r3.claim: Correct investigators leave the duration to God, as the sleepers do; accordingly, the Prophet did not specify the Mahdi's appearance date.

QASHANI:18:12/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:12/r4.speaker: عليه السلام
QASHANI:18:12/r4.claim: A prophetic report condemns people who set dates, supporting refusal to specify the Mahdi's appearance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r6.claim: Aḥṣā means to preserve and record accurately.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r1.claim: The two groups most likely are the youths themselves, as their later exchange shows; those saying the Lord knows best had realized the long duration, and the Quran first summarizes then retells the story at length.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj and al-Tabrīzī prefer the elative reading; al-Fārisī, al-Zamakhsharī, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefer a past verb, citing the normal pattern for forms of comparison and exclamation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r11.claim: Abū Isḥāq says elative forms from quadriliteral verbs have become common and are therefore permissible; Ibn ʿAṭiyya misclassifies examples such as aswad and abyad, which are not quadriliteral.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r12.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r12.claim: Three positions govern comparative and exclamatory afʿal: Sībawayh’s apparent view permits it freely, another allows none except anomalous forms, and a third permits it when the hamza is not causative.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, reporting the majority, says one group was the youths who thought they had stayed briefly and the other was the city people who had kept a record of them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r3.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says the two arguing groups were Jews and Christians who prompted Quraysh to ask about the cave youths, al-Khiḍr, and the spirit; they disagreed about the duration.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says believers and unbelievers among the cave people disagreed about how long they stayed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the groups were believers living in the youths’ time, disputing the duration.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies one group with the successive rulers of the city and the other with the cave people.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r7.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r7.claim: Ibn Baḥr says the two groups are God and creatures, like the question ‘Are you more knowledgeable or God?’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r8.claim: The author calls these alternatives confused; Ibn Qatāda instead says neither believers nor unbelievers knew the duration, while Muqātil says waking ended the uncertainty and disclosed its truth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r9.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqā allow aḥṣā as a past verb with mā as a verbal noun and amadan as object, or as an elative with amadan as specification.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r1.claim: The majority read linaʿlama with first-person plural; al-Zuhrī and a report in Ibn Khalawayh read it with yāʾ, and al-Akhfash also reports liyaʿlam.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r2.claim: Baʿathnāhum means waking them from sleep; baʿth is movement from stillness in a person or from the state in which it had been sent.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r3.claim: Linaʿlama means to make their already known matter manifest, as discussed for the parallel ‘so We may know who follows the Messenger.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r4.speaker: الزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r4.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads the verb with yāʾ; in al-Kashshāf this reading omits an object and suspends the clause as the predicate of a nominal phrase.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r5.claim: The author rejects al-Kashshāf’s passive-like clausal analysis under Basran grammar: a full sentence cannot serve as the substitute for an already omitted passive subject; Kufans allow either any spoken clause or only one that permits suspension.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p145/r6.claim: The nun reading may shift from divine first person to third-person reference without changing the meaning; with yāʾ, the omitted first object is God’s making people know which group, while the nominal clause supplies the next two objects.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r1.claim: If أحصى is a noun of comparison, أي الحزبين can be a relative built under Sībawayh’s rule because the beginning of its relative clause is omitted; if أحصى is a past verb, that condition fails.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r2.claim: He rejects taking أحصى as أفعل التفضيل: formation from a non-triliteral root is not regular, and the cited irregular examples cannot establish a Qurʾānic rule.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r3.claim: The objection that a comparative cannot govern أمدا is wrong: comparatives govern specification, so أمدا can be a tamyīz, as in أقطع الناس سيفا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r4.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī parses أمدا with لبثوا, though Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls that analysis ill-directed; Abū Ḥayyān says it can work if the phrase means the duration’s endpoint.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p146/r5.claim: He finds the construction with لبثوا possible: أمدا means a term or duration, with an omitted preposition, لما لبثوا من أمد, comparable to Qurʾānic مِنْ constructions.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r1.claim: Kūfan grammarians allow an أفعل comparative to take a direct object; Basrans explain such examples through an implied verbal noun, and some grammarians analyze أعلم من يضل similarly.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p148/r2.claim: If examples such as أضرب منا بالسيوف القوانسا were common, analogy would be valid because the comparative contains the meaning of a verbal noun and the sense is sound.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r1.claim: When أحصى is nominal, the Shaikh allows أي to be relative, with أحصى predicate of an omitted relative clause; a past-tense parse has no basis for building أي.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r2.claim: The relative analysis requires علم to mean recognition, leaving only one object; attributing this sense to God raises a separate issue.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's example of أضرب منا بالسيوف القوانسا is challenged; the Shaikh says Kufi grammar allows Af'al itself to govern a complement.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r4.claim: The Shaikh cites a Kufan account of أضرب governing القوانس and analogizes أعلم من يضل; the author says this position is weak.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r5.claim: A second parse of أحصى as a past verb makes أمدا its object, with لما لبثوا attached or circumstantial; alternative parses make its ل زائد.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r6.claim: The Shaikh argues أمدا can be a tamyiz under the past verb; he also says dropping من before an explanatory أمد gives a viable “duration” sense.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r7.claim: The author cautions that al-Tabari may have intended tamyiz rather than direct-object governance by لبثوا.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses أمدا as object under the verbal reading, with لما لبثوا as adjective, circumstantial, or causal; elsewhere it may be supplied by an implied verb.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#2/r9.claim: A “for the duration they remained” analysis treats ما as relative and drops من before أمدا; Ibn Atiyya calls direct governance by لبثوا ill-directed.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r1.claim: The author says Kufi government of القوانس by أفعل is a weak comparative analysis.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r2.claim: With nominal أحصى, أي may be relative and أحصى the predicate of an omitted relative clause, with a built ending under Sibawayh's conditions.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r3.claim: That account only works if علم means recognition; otherwise the single object is insufficient, and divine recognition raises a separate issue.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12#3/r4.claim: If أحصى is a verb, أي cannot be relative because there is no reason for it to be built.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r1.claim: لنعلم attaches to the awakening; the majority use first-person plural in continuity with the discourse.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r10.claim: Alternatively, أحصى is a past verb with أمدا as object; Abu Ali, al-Zamakhshari, and Ibn Atiyya choose this parse.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari objects that non-triliteral comparatives are irregular and أمدا has no satisfactory governor or sense on that parse.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r12.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r12.claim: The Shaikh answers that views differ: Sibawayh allows أفعل, al-Farisi forbids it, and another view allows it when hamza is not causative, as here.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r13.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r13.claim: He says أفعل governs a tamyiz such as سيفا in أقطع الناس سيفا; the author objects that duration is not what performs the counting.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r14.claim: أمدا cannot be tamyiz because counting is an attribute of the groups, not the period itself.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r15.claim: The Shaikh explains that أمد is a duration or limit and cites 2:106 and 35:2 for من explaining an indefinite ما.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r16.claim: The author calls comparative أفعل weak in this use because it lacks the inflection of a participial adjective.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r2.speaker: الزهري
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri reads ليعلم with third-person ياء and God as subject, a shift to third person.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r3.claim: If أي الحزبين is relative, it may be the subject of ليعلم.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r4.claim: For passive ليعلم, al-Zamakhshari makes the content of the following clause نائب فاعل; the Shaikh says this is not Basran usage.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r5.claim: Kufans permit clauses in this role, generally or when they are content complements; if أي الحزبين is relative it can itself be subject.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r6.claim: A reading with damma on ياء has God as subject and an omitted first object الناس; أي الحزبين supplies the second or both, depending on the sense of علم.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r7.claim: أحصى may be a comparative adjective predicate of interrogative أيهم; the clause suspends علم and لما لبثوا is circumstantial to أمدا.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r8.claim: In that parse, لِما may be causal or extra; ما may be governed by أحصى or an implied verb; أمدا may be object of لبثوا or an implied governor.

SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:12/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Tabrizi prefer the comparative parse.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r2.claim: God raised them from sleep, and one later went out with their money to buy food.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p139#2/r3.claim: The two parties differed over their time in the cave; amad may mean the number of years or the final limit or endpoint.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r14.claim: God awakened them so that their situation and the competing groups' estimates would become manifest to observers, though God already knew it unseen.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r15.claim: The two groups are the sleepers and those who later encountered them; the latter estimated duration from their coins or other clues.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r16.claim: Their estimate of a day or part of one could be close to the truth but remained conjectural, unlike God's certain knowledge.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p448/r17.claim: The groups' ignorance of the sleepers' duration demonstrates God's perfect knowledge and that He has neither child nor partner in rule.

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r3.claim: The two parties were the people of guidance and the people of error among the youths' community; they had recorded the date of their departure to count their stay.

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r4.claim: The two parties were groups from the youths' people, and أحصى means that they counted the duration as a number.

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r5.claim: Neither group, whether the pagans or believers, knew how long the sleepers had remained.

BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r1.claim: God awakened them from heavy sleep resembling death, showing that sleep shares death’s suspension of life and is followed by resurrection.

BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r2.claim: ‘That We may know’ means testing, named by its result; such a test need not produce the tested action and can expose inability, as in the command to bring the sun from the west.

BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the two parties as the youths and the successive kings who ruled their city.

BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r4.claim: The phrase asks which group best counted the stay; ahṣā is past tense meaning counted, not a comparative, and amad means duration or endpoint.

BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p170#2/r5.claim: The test shows both parties’ inability to count, leading them to entrust the matter to God, recognize His preservation of bodies and faith, and gain certainty in His power, knowledge, and resurrection.

BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r1.claim: The cave youths fled Daqyanus, while seekers in retreat long for encounter with God; they seek rescue from the self and escape from existence’s darkness into divine beauty and majesty.

BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p170#3/r5.claim: ‘Then We raised them’ means God gave them life through Him; the two parties are cave dwellers and retreat seekers, each asking which correctly measured its stay.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r1.claim: The awakening means that God roused them and stirred them from sleep.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r10.claim: He reads ahsa as a past-tense verb meaning “measured precisely,” with ay as its subject; al-Farisi, al-Zamakhshari, and Ibn Atiyya choose this too.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r11.claim: On the preferred parsing, ma is a verbal noun, the prepositional phrase is an advanced circumstantial phrase, and amadan is the object of ahsa.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r12.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r12.claim: Al-Raghib defines amad as a bounded period; unlike zaman, it is considered with regard to its endpoint, while another lexicographer says amad and mada are close.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r13.claim: The question concerns counting the duration as discrete units, dividing it into years and reaching a numerical count, not measuring its continuous extent.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r14.claim: An alternative takes amad as the duration's endpoint: the count may concern the full 309 years or the final, three-hundred-ninth year, with the latter counting the number's encompassed ranks.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r15.claim: Some take amad literally as the duration and figuratively as its endpoint; either sense can be defended by construing the duration as an ongoing state with a limit.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r2.claim: The first party may be those who said they stayed a day or part of one, and the second those who said God knew best.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya says most commentators identify the two parties as the youths who guessed briefly and the people of the city, who knew their absence's duration from records.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the parties as the sleepers and the successive kings who ruled the city.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says the two parties were believers and unbelievers among the people of the cave.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r6.claim: Al-Farra says both parties were believers living in the same era who disagreed about how long the sleepers remained.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r7.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddi identifies both parties as unbelievers: Jews and Christians who informed Quraysh about asking the Prophet concerning the cave.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r8.speaker: ابن حرب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r8.claim: Ibn Harb identifies the two parties as God and creation, invoking the question, “Are you more knowing, or God?”

ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p212#2/r9.claim: The author prefers the parties already mentioned in the exchange, since the definite article points back to them and supplies no other antecedent.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r1.claim: Allowing ma to be verbal under the preceding analysis is possible but remote; adding lam is also weak because it is not added in such a construction.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r10.claim: A past-tense verb does not imply knowledge of the count before awakening; the past reflects the time of narration.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r11.claim: A final objection says the comparative implies both parties had counted and one was simply more accurate, though the story shows otherwise.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r12.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r12.claim: Al-Kashf says al-Zajjaj's view is not so objectionable, but al-Zamakhshari's preferred reading is better in wording and meaning because the parties were discussing, not ranking expertise.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Tabrizi read ahsa as a comparative, supported by comparable Qur’anic comparisons and their view that awakening cannot aim at a count completed before it.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r3.claim: One objection is that comparatives from non-triliteral verbs are not regular; grammarians variously allow them, forbid them except as anomalies, or allow them when the hamza is not causative.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh apparently permits forming a comparative from non-triliteral verbs without restriction.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r5.claim: Abu Ali forbids such formation except for anomalous forms, which cannot serve as a productive pattern.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r6.speaker: ابن عصفور
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r6.claim: Ibn Asfur distinguishes causative hamza, which blocks comparative formation, from other hamza; here the hamza is not causative.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r7.claim: A second objection asks how the comparative can govern amadan as a direct object; supplying an omitted verb merely repeats the text, while other parses distort the sense.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan treats amadan as a duration governed by a dropped preposition: the original would mean “for a duration”; ma explicates an otherwise vague word.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213#2/r9.claim: The objection that a comparative cannot take a direct object reflects Basran grammar, not Kufan grammar; nevertheless the proposed reading makes amadan a specification, which comparatives can govern.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r1.claim: Al-Raghib's clear lexical usage makes duration the literal sense of amad and endpoint figurative; forcing the endpoint reading is unnecessary when ma is verbal.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r2.claim: If ma is a relative pronoun instead, its omitted relative pronoun means “the time in which they stayed.”

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r3.claim: A proposed purpose-clause reading of ma, with the lam added because the clause is neither a verbal noun nor simultaneous, is weak.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r4.claim: Another analysis makes lam extra and ma a relative object, with amadan an accusative specification transferred from the object: originally, “count the duration of their time.”

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r5.claim: The objection that a specification must derive from a subject is unfounded: recognized grammars allow it to derive from an object, as in the earth being made to burst into springs.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p213/r6.claim: A specification of relation is not a specification of an individual noun, and grammarians do not require the latter to be transformed from a subject.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r1.claim: Ay is an interrogative subject followed by its predicate; in this construction it suspends the verb naʿlam from taking its normal object.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r2.claim: If ahsa is a comparative, ay may be a relative pronoun built as a noun of relation because its relative clause has its opening pronoun omitted; it cannot be built that way with a finite verb.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r3.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r3.claim: Al-Zuhri reads liyaʿlama with a yāʾ, shifting the attribution of the action to God in a grammatical turn.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r4.claim: God's knowledge as the aim of awakening is not literal, which would imply the false claim attributed to Hisham.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r5.claim: One explanation reads “know” as a metaphor for making the truth manifest or distinguishing the parties; another makes divine knowledge newly related to an event after it occurs.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r6.claim: The second explanation is compared to testing who follows the Messenger and who turns back after the change of prayer direction.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r7.claim: A critic objects that awakening did not divide the parties into accurate counters and non-counters, unlike the changed prayer direction, which separated followers from deserters.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r8.claim: The critic instead treats the wording as a test: God exposes their inability to know the duration, so they defer to Him, gain certainty in resurrection, and become a sign to believers and deniers.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p214/r9.claim: The author rejects portraying God as awakening them like someone who wants to discover an unknown result, since that might suggest desire necessitates fulfillment.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p215/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p215/r1.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p215/r1.claim: Al-Khafaji says a real test is impossible for an all-knowing God and that calling it a metaphor returns to the rejected claim; he reads knowledge as a metonym for public manifestation.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p215/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p215/r2.speaker: الخفاجي
